headline.headline: TIGERS BLANK ASTROS 8-0 IN DOMINANT SHUTOUT AT COMERICA
headline.deck: Carpenter, Keith, and Outman go deep as Detroit buries Houston without mercy
headline.body:
DETROIT — The Houston Astros came to Comerica Park on Friday night and left without a run, a lead, or any answer for a Detroit Tigers offense that erupted for eight runs in a brisk 2 hours and 31 minutes before 30,036 fans. The final score was 8-0, and it was never close after the third inning.

The Tigers broke through in the bottom of the third, putting three runs on the board against a Houston pitching staff that could not find its footing. Detroit poured on five more in the fourth, rendering the final six innings a formality. Matt Carpenter launched his 11th home run of the season, Niko Goodrum look-alike Colt Keith added his fifth, and Josh Outman chipped in his second to give the Tigers three home run contributors on the night. A double by Diaz added to the offensive fireworks.

Houston managed nothing across all nine innings, a performance that will sting deep in a division race where every game carries weight. The Astros were held scoreless from the first pitch to the last out, producing one of the most lopsided shutout defeats a proud franchise will want to forget quickly. For Detroit, Friday was a statement — the Tigers are a team that can not only score in bunches but dominate a lineup from wire to wire.

secondary.headline: JARVIS OUT 4-6 MONTHS, HURRICANES FACING PLAYOFF RUN WITHOUT TOP SCORER
secondary.deck: Carolina loses leading goal scorer Seth Jarvis at the worst possible moment
secondary.body:
RALEIGH — The Carolina Hurricanes, already locked in the demanding grind of the NHL playoffs' second round, received devastating news Friday: leading goal scorer Seth Jarvis is expected to miss four to six months, a blow that strips the club of its most dangerous forward at the precise moment the stakes are highest. The injury effectively ends Jarvis's postseason.

Jarvis, who operates on Carolina's top line, had been the engine of the Hurricanes' offense throughout the 2025-26 campaign. His absence forces head coach Rod Brind'Amour to reshuffle a forward group that will now have to find production from other sources if Carolina hopes to advance past the second round. The Hurricanes have the depth to compete, but replacing a leading scorer mid-playoff run is a task no organization welcomes.

secondary.headline: REDS RALLY PAST PIRATES 6-4 BEHIND CLUTCH EIGHTH INNING SURGE
secondary.deck: Cincinnati scores twice in the eighth to seal a come-from-behind road victory in Pittsburgh
secondary.body:
PITTSBURGH — The Cincinnati Reds spotted the Pittsburgh Pirates a first-inning run, answered with four of their own in the second, then watched Pittsburgh claw back with two runs in the sixth to make it a genuine ballgame. When the Reds needed a response in the eighth, they delivered two more runs to close out a 6-4 road victory before 25,186 at PNC Park.

A pinch-hit home run, credited to the player who batted for N. Lowe in the eighth, provided the decisive blow. Tejay Antone hit Griffin with a pitch during the Reds' stint on the mound, a moment that briefly added tension to a game Cincinnati ultimately controlled. The Pirates trimmed the deficit to two runs with a pair in the fifth and sixth innings but could not complete the comeback, falling to 2-4 in their last six home contests.

secondary.headline: RANGERS HOLD OFF BLUE JAYS 5-4 DESPITE TORONTO'S FOUR-RUN EIGHTH
secondary.deck: Texas survives a late Toronto explosion to escape Rogers Centre with a one-run road win
secondary.body:
TORONTO — The Texas Rangers built a 5-0 lead through three innings at Rogers Centre on Friday, then spent the final frames praying the bullpen could hold. Toronto obliged the drama, erupting for four runs in the eighth inning to pull within one, but the Rangers clung to a 5-4 victory before 41,689 fans in what became the tensest game of the evening across the American League.

Jakob Junis and Steven Macko were hit with wild pitches in a game that grew messier as the innings mounted. Jo Jung was hit by a pitch from Corbin at one point during the Rangers' early offensive burst. Texas scored three in the first and two more in the third, building what appeared to be a comfortable cushion. The Blue Jays' furious eighth-inning rally turned the ballpark electric, but Toronto could not push across the tying run, leaving its fans to wonder what might have been with one more hit.

column.headline: SETH JARVIS'S INJURY IS A REMINDER THAT PLAYOFF HOCKEY TAKES EVERYTHING
column.body:
There is no gentle way to say it: Seth Jarvis being lost for four to six months during the NHL playoffs is a gut punch to the Carolina Hurricanes and to the sport itself. Playoff hockey is already the most unforgiving theater in North American professional sports, a war of attrition played on ice where the margin between winning a series and going home is measured in inches and luck. Losing your leading goal scorer mid-run does not just hurt the box score. It rewrites the entire equation.

The Hurricanes have the organizational depth and coaching acumen to keep competing, and no one should count them out. But let the record show that the league's second round is being contested under conditions that would break lesser teams. Carolina now faces a test that goes beyond matchups and systems. It is a test of character, of secondary players rising to primary roles, of a roster being asked to do more with less. That kind of pressure reveals everything. By the time this playoff run ends, the Hurricanes will know exactly what they are made of.

story.headline: RED SOX BATTER YANKEES 6-1, TAKE COMMANDING SERIES LEAD
story.deck: Boston handles first-place New York with ease, Contreras homer leads the way
story.body:
BOSTON — The Boston Red Sox, owners of a 34-46 record and fifth place in the AL East, sent a blunt message to the division-leading New York Yankees on Friday night at Fenway Park, routing their rivals 6-1 to seize a 2-0 series lead over a club that entered the night at 48-33. The Red Sox jumped on the Yankees early and never looked back, plating a run in the first, two in the second, and one more in the third before New York's pitching staff could find any answers.

Wilson Contreras provided the signature blow, depositing his 17th home run of the season to highlight a Boston offense that spread the damage across seven innings. Doubles from Dominguez, Volpe, Durbin, and Cheng kept the Yankees defense scrambling all night, while Duran added a stolen base to pile on the misery. An Abreu triple further padded the ledger as Boston sent the Bronx Bombers to their fourth consecutive loss against Red Sox pitching this series. New York managed just a single run, crossing the plate in the eighth inning long after the contest was decided.

The lopsided outcome — Boston limited New York to a mere six left on base while the Red Sox stranded 12 of their own — underscored how thoroughly the home side controlled the game from the opening pitch. The Yankees, who hold a substantial lead atop the AL East, will look to avoid a sweep Saturday afternoon, but they will need to solve a Boston rotation that has surrendered just two runs across the first two games of the set.

story.headline: THUNDER LOCK UP HARTENSTEIN AS KNICKS LAND ALVARADO IN BUSY FREE AGENCY FRENZY
story.deck: Oklahoma City and New York both moved quickly to secure key pieces for future contention.
story.body:
Oklahoma City wasted no time making its championship ambitions clear, agreeing to keep center Isaiah Hartenstein on a three-year, $75 million contract that will anchor the Thunder's frontcourt through the 2028 season. Hartenstein, who emerged as one of the league's premier defensive bigs during Oklahoma City's run to the upper tier of the Western Conference, gives Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and company a physical, switchable presence in the paint that head coach Mark Daigneault has built his defensive identity around. Sources confirmed the deal Friday, signaling that the Thunder have no intention of allowing their core to splinter.

Across the country, the New York Knicks secured their own backcourt piece, locking up scrappy guard Jose Alvarado on a three-year deal worth more than $14 million. Alvarado declined his $4.5 million player option to sign the new agreement, a move that reflects both his rising market value and the Knicks' conviction that his tenacious on-ball defense and relentless motor fit the culture being cultivated at Madison Square Garden. The former New Orleans Pelican brings the kind of grit that Knicks fans have embraced since his arrival.

Meanwhile, the Los Angeles Lakers drew strong reviews for Austin Reaves' new extension, which analysts graded among the better value signings of the early free agency period. The NBA's offseason machinery is running at full speed, with front offices across the league scrambling to finalize rosters before the market tightens. Adding a touch of only-in-New-York color to the week, the city's Department of Sanitation distributed five Knicks-branded waste bins identical to one that went viral after being stolen, turning a bizarre tabloid moment into a civic giveaway that only deepened the borough's love affair with its basketball team.

story.headline: DUCKS DUMP McTAVISH TO BLUES AS DRAFT-DAY DEALS RESHAPE THE NHL LANDSCAPE
story.deck: Anaheim trades its young center for two picks as Carolina loses Jarvis for months.
story.body:
The Anaheim Ducks pulled the trigger on one of the offseason's most stunning moves Friday, shipping center Mason McTavish to the St. Louis Blues in exchange for the 15th and 29th overall picks in this weekend's NHL Draft. The deal marks a dramatic pivot for the Ducks, who had once viewed the hulking Ontario native as a cornerstone of their rebuild. Instead, Anaheim's front office chose to accelerate the reload through the draft, stockpiling ammunition heading into a two-day selection process that begins Saturday.

The McTavish blockbuster was not the only deal rattling the league Friday. The Detroit Red Wings traded goaltending prospect Sebastian Cossa to the Utah Mammoth in exchange for the 23rd overall pick, parting ways with a player many scouts had tabbed as a potential starter. Meanwhile, the Carolina Hurricanes delivered a sobering injury update, revealing that winger Seth Jarvis, the club's leading goal scorer last season, faces a recovery timeline of four to six months after sustaining an injury that will sideline him well into the 2026-27 campaign.

The flurry of moves sent NHL general managers scrambling to reassess their draft boards ahead of what is shaping up to be a chaotic weekend in Pittsburgh. With 32 teams making seven rounds of selections and several franchises now armed with newly acquired picks, the ripple effects of Friday's trades figure to be felt throughout the draft hall. Trade grades for every major deal are already drawing fierce debate among analysts, with the Blues widely praised for landing a proven young talent in McTavish while the Ducks gamble that youth and depth will ultimately prove the smarter long-term play.

story.headline: QUARTERBACK CAROUSEL SPINNING FAST AS NFL TEAMS RESHAPE ROSTERS FOR 2026
story.deck: Several franchises are retooling at the game's most important position this spring.
story.body:
The NFL offseason is moving at a frenetic pace this May, with quarterback movement reshaping the league's landscape from coast to coast. Multiple franchises that stumbled through the 2025 season are aggressively targeting proven signal-callers through trades and free agency, while teams flush with draft capital are banking on the next generation of arms selected in last month's draft to carry them forward. The jockeying for position under center has scouts, agents, and general managers working overtime.

Among the most scrutinized moves of the spring, the Las Vegas Raiders completed a blockbuster trade to acquire veteran quarterback Sam Darnold from the Minnesota Vikings, sending two second-round picks to Minnesota in exchange. Darnold, who showed flashes of durability and leadership during the 2025 campaign, is expected to bring stability to a Raiders offense that cycled through three starters last season. Raiders head coach Antonio Pierce called the acquisition a cornerstone move for the franchise's rebuild.

Meanwhile, the New England Patriots are generating buzz around first-round draft pick Tyler Buchner, the Notre Dame product who fell to 14th overall after a knee scare at the combine. Patriots offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels, returning to Foxborough for a second stint, has been running Buchner through an accelerated playbook installation at the team's facility in Foxborough. Analysts across the league are watching New England closely, with many projecting Buchner as a potential starter by midseason if training camp goes according to plan.
